arguments.decision: How should the shipped clean-code skill (plugins/code/skills/clean-code), which users copy into their own projects and which the user has now decided to move from Deno to Node.js, reach its dependencies and the Deno APIs its scripts call?
arguments.evidence: The user decided on 2026-09-29 (through the develop session) that the clean-code skill moves to Node so that Deno is no longer required anywhere in the repository, that @deno/shim-deno is kept where it is used, and that the report must state what skill users must install (Node version, any npm install step). The skill has SKILL.md, deno.json (imports: eslint 10.10.0, typescript-eslint 8.70.0, typescript 6.0.3, @typescript-eslint/utils 8.70.0 from npm; @std/fs 1.0.24, @std/path 1.1.6, @std/assert 1, @cliffy/command 1.2.1 from JSR), deno.lock, and three scripts. Its runtime scripts call the Deno namespace at 5 sites: clean_code.ts Deno.args, Deno.cwd and Deno.readTextFile; cli.ts Deno.args and Deno.exitCode. Its test file clean_code_test.ts has 5 Deno.test registrations and about 20 Deno file-system calls. Today users run 'deno run --config <skill-root>/deno.json --lock <skill-root>/deno.lock --frozen --cached-only --no-prompt --allow-read --allow-env <skill-root>/scripts/clean_code.ts --scope'. The repository's own scripts import the skill's cli.ts and run with the repository preload (scripts/deno_shim.ts, which bridges Deno.exitCode). JSR packages install through npm only from npm.jsr.io with a project .npmrc containing @jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io and allow-remote=root (npm 12 refuses them otherwise). Node runs the .ts files with type stripping; clean_code.ts uses import.meta.main.

candidates.description: The skill gets its own package.json, package-lock.json and .npmrc (the same pinned packages as npm and JSR aliases, plus @deno/shim-deno) and its own copy of the preload; its Deno call sites stay unchanged except Deno.test, and users run 'npm ci --prefix <skill-root>' once and then 'node --import <skill-root>/scripts/deno_shim.ts <skill-root>/scripts/clean_code.ts --scope'.

The skill gets its own package.json, package-lock.json and .npmrc (the same pinned packages as npm and JSR aliases, no shim); its few Deno call sites are rewritten to Node built-ins (process.argv, process.cwd, node:fs/promises, process.exitCode, node:test), and users run 'npm ci --prefix <skill-root>' once and then 'node <skill-root>/scripts/clean_code.ts --scope'.

requirements: Users run the skill with one plain node command after one npm install step.
Adds no new copy of locally owned glue code to the shipped skill.
arguments.priorities:
User and repository priorities (verbose-broccoli, feature/turborepo, Linear CHE-32, a trial whose result is a report; nothing is merged):
1. The user chose to move the TypeScript side from Deno to Node.js and to run the three Python packages (backfire, doc-regions, wiki-consistency) as one native uv workspace under Turborepo's experimental Python support.
2. Change only the parts that must change; leave everything else as it is. The smallest change that reaches the goal wins.
3. AGENTS.md reuse order: first existing repository, runtime, standard-library or dependency functionality; then a stable upstream dependency; then an unstable upstream with the smallest patch; last, minimal glue. Minimize locally owned code; prefer reducing locally owned implementation over reducing dependency count. If the goal needs substantial new local implementation, stop and report instead.
4. Requirements that stay: built backfire plugins install offline, stay self-contained and write only into their own .venv; readiness proves the server runs from its own .venv.
5. The user decided on 2026-09-29 to move the shipped clean-code skill to Node too, so that Deno is not required anywhere in the repository, keeping @deno/shim-deno where it is used.
6. Dropping a check, changing scope, changing governance documents, or changing the user's global tools (Node, npm, uv, Codex) is the user's decision, not the agent's.
